description.narrative: The Program Development Objective is to contribute to reducing key risks for non-communicable and infectious diseases, including COVID-19, and improving efficiency of health services in Moldova.

The objective of the Health Transformation Operation Project for Moldova is to contribute to reducing key risks for non-communicable diseases and improving efficiency of health services in Moldova. The project will be a Program for Results, or PforR operation with a technical assistance component (Investment Project Financing, or IPF, with implementation details in annex eight). This will follow the existing fiduciary framework in the country. The program will be implemented by the Ministry of Health, or MOH and National Health Insurance Company, or CNAM, and both will be conducting procurement and financial management on their own as each have the established structures and the required authority. Every TT has three accounts within the Treasury Account, or TSA corresponding to the budget components: (i) one for state budget - main component; (ii) one for state budget - special means and special funds; and (iii) for ATU budget.

title.narrative: Intermediate Results Indicator 5: Annual hospitalizations through referrals by family medicine providers
PDO Indicator 1: Smoking prevalence among adults

comment.narrative:
<p><strong>NOT ACHIEVED</strong></p>

<p><u>Baseline and data source:</u> </p>

<p>In the approved PAD, the baseline for this indicator was temporary, with an explicitly stated intention to use the published data from the 2013 STEPS survey as the baseline, when available. Field data collection for the STEPS Survey was completed in November 2013, but the final results were not published until June 2014. Additional STEPS surveys were envisioned in Year 2 and Year 4 of Program implementation. However, there were persistent delays in MoHLSP contracting WHO to carry out the STEPS survey. The contract was eventually signed in February 2019, with the survey scheduled to be carried out in early 2020. However, this was further delayed due to the COVID-19 pandemic. In this context, an agreement was reached with the National Bureau of Statistics (NBS) to add a health module (including tobacco consumption) to their household survey and the baseline, target and data source were revised in the second restructuring (December 2020). </p>

<p><u>Data issues:</u></p>

<p>1) At the time of Project approval (April 2014), a baseline of 28% was used, with a baseline date of 2008 listed. While no source of data was provided, a Demographic and Health Survey was conducted in 2005 and reported that the rate of daily smoking was 28% and, therefore, <em>may<em> </em></em>????have been the original data source.??? </p>

<p>2) At the time of the first restructuring (October 2018), and in line with the 2013 STEPS survey for the population aged 18-69, the baseline was revised to 25.4%. Sub-indicator baselines were as follows: 43.5% for men, 5.7% for women. This daa differed slightly from that reported in the 2013 STEPS (Table 11), which reported an overall prevalence of 25.3%, and prevalence among men and women at 43.6% and 5.6%, respectively.  </p>

<p>3) At the time of the second restructuring (December 2020), the team further revised the baseline due to the delay in follow-up STEPS survey due to COVID-19, which would not allow for endline data compared to the baseline based on the 2013 STEPS survey. However, the source for the revised data was not specified. In the January 2020 Aide Memoire, it was noted that a 'new methodology will be used based on GPS mapping of households.' However, it is unlear how the baseline was determined during the restructuring when the methodology for measurement appears to have still have been under discussion. Later, in the June 2022 Aide Memoire, it was noted that the NBS had been contracted to add a health module to the household survey, including tobacco consumption.</p>

<p>Based on the 2022 NBS household survey and team reporting, smoking prevalence among adults was estimated at 14.7% as of April 2022. While this data is consistent with one figure (Figure 11), it is not consistent with the more detailed data presented in Table 69, which notes an overall prevalence for the population over the age of 15 that report smoking daily of 12.3% (24.1% for men, 2.6% for  women). Upon further investigation, similar data for 2013 an 2017 show the following: 2013 - 13% prevalence (27.2% for men, 2.3% for women); 2017 - 12.8% prevalence (25.5% for men, 2.7% for women). Despite the lack of clarity regarding the source of the baseline data, based on data reported by the NBS from 2013-2017, a slight decline in overall smoking prevalence from 13% to 12.3% is observed. Given that this was the agreed data source at the time of Program closure, it has been entered above in the Results Framework. </p>

<p>Sources:</p>

<p>1) 2013 (Table 43): https://statistica.gov.md/files/files/publicatii_electronice/acces_servicii_sanatate/Acces_servicii_sanatate_editia_2013.pdf</p>

<p>2) 2017 (Table A45): https://statistica.gov.md/public/files/publicatii_electronice/acces_servicii_sanatate/Acces_servicii_sanatate_2016.pdf</p>

<p>3) 2022 (Table 69):

<p>The decline in discharges represents a 41.7% reduction compared to the original target.</p>

<p>Data was calculated according to the Annual CNAM Report for 2020, using the indicator of a stable population of 3,545,124 according to the National Public Health Agency. Annual acute care hospital discharges were calculated based on CNAM data provided (the data include a number of treated, reported, and validated acute cases for 2021).</p>

Intermediate Results Indicator 2: Revision of the outpatient drug benefit package with regard to antihypertensive drugs

comment.narrative:
<p><strong>ACHIEVED.</strong></p>

<p>Starting February 1, 2019, citizens have been able to request medications free of charge (only one from each INN, the cost of which falls within the compensated amounts established quarterly by CNAM), according to Order No. 96/20A dated January 24th, 2019 signed by the Ministry of Health, Labor and Social Protection and CNAM.</p>

<p>Starting with October 1, 2021, the methodology of compensated fixed amount calculation has been changed. Thus, according to the joint Order of MoH and CNAM No. 933/255 from October 8, 2021, for all partially reimbursed medicines (40%, 80%, 90%) have been applied the reimbursement rate of 100% at the median fixed market price.</p>

<p>The total number of INN for CVDs in the benefits package has steadily increased: 25 INN (2019); 26 INN (2020); 27 INN (2021); 27 INN (2022) and 29 INN (2023).</p>

title.narrative: Intermediate Results Indicator 1: Approval of the new tobacco control legislation

comment.narrative:
<p><strong>ACHIEVED</strong></p>

<p>The national Tobacco Control Law was approved in May 2015 and entered into force in September 2015. The law stipulates: (i) bans tobacco advertising (starting January 2016); (ii) bans smoking in enclosed public spaces (starting May 2016); (iii) prohibits artificial flavor additives in cigarettes (starting 2018); (iv) introduced traceability for cigarettes packs (starting 2018); (v) requires the labeling of cigarettes packs with health warning messages (starting2018). In addition, it also established a set of sanctions for violations of the regulations.</p>

<p>The Tobacco Control Law was further amended in 2019 to include a specific excise rate of for heated tobacco (effective August 16, 2019). Cigarettes continue to be subject to a mixed excise system that includes an ad-valorem tax based on the retail price, a specific tax and a minimumtotal excise based on sticks. Since 2020, the ad-valorem tax on cigarettes is 13% of the retail price. Therefore, the excise rate on heated tobacco is effectively equal to the minimum excise on cigarettes.  </p>

PDO Indicator 6: Revise the national communication strategy for COVID-19 (based on the results of the survey and the Vaccines Readiness Assessment) and implement six activities of the revised strategy

comment.narrative:
<p><strong>ACHIEVED</strong></p>

<p>The Program supported a robust health systems assessment. Purchasing vaccines is just one stepin a multi-dimensional effort that involves detailed planning and implementation of a vaccine deployment program. This includes a variety of issues, such as effective microplanning, safe and appropriate transportation, storage, training, ancillary materials, registration, and a suitable information management system. In this context, the assessment was the product of a multi-partner effort that provided a comprehensive assessment of Moldova’s readiness to deliver COVID-19 vaccines, including critical gaps and measures to address them. Informed by assessment findings, a national COVID-19 vaccine deployment plan was developed and adopted by the Government in January 2021.</p>

<p>The Program also studied behavioral insights related to COVID-19 vaccination and supported COVID-19-related communications activities. Specifically, the implementation of a survey of behavioral insights on COVID-19 in Moldova provided insights on potential and existing gaps in vaccine acceptance. This important work revealed that about 31 percent of the population was likely to accept a safe and effective COVID-19 vaccine, while 70 percent had concerns about vaccine safety and 24 percent did not believe that COVID-19 was real.</p>

<p>With Program support, as well as support from UNICEF, the MoHLSP revised the NationalCOVID-19 Communication Strategy based on the results of the Vaccines Readiness Assessment Framework and the study on behavior insights to COVID-19 vaccination. The revised strategy focused on activities to increase vaccine uptake and reduce disinformation. Specifically, it included a detailed action plan that specified strategic communication channels (including video spots, interviews, articles, and social network postings on vaccination of health workers) and dissemination events (including press conferences and briefings). The action plan identified timelines and responsible agencies for key activities. The communications strategy specified target groups, monitoring and evaluating framework, and mechanisms for addressing vaccine hesitancy, misinformation, and false rumors.</p>

<p>Between June 2020 and August 2021, 44 activities were implemented covering a diverse array of topics and delivered using a number of different communications platforms. Communications focused on increasing awareness about COVID-19 (including through sharing stories from front-line workers), disseminating information on safe hygiene and public health measures, promoting COVID-19 vaccination, and combatting COVID-19-related disinformation, among others. Communication types employed included print, broadcast and social media, as well as face-to-face events. </p>
